item.title: [10] Light-induced asymmetric pseudogap below the critical temperature in cuprates
item.description:
Last authors: A. J. Millis, F. Boschini

Authors: D. Armanno, O. Gingras, F. Goto, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct tr-ARPES study of competing pseudogap and superconducting states in optimally doped cuprates.

Tags: #tr-ARPES #cuprates #superconductivity #pseudogap

Abstract: High-temperature cuprate superconductors remain a key platform for studying the competition and coexistence of emergent quantum phases of matter. These include non-s-wave superconductivity with a high transition temperature, non-Fermi-liquid transport and the pseudogap regime. How superconductivity emerges alongside and competes with the pseudogap remains an open question. Here, by directly accessing the near-antinodal region of optimally doped Bi-based cuprates via time- and angle-resolved photoemission, we report a transient change from a symmetric superconducting-like density of states to an asymmetric pseudogap-like density of states when superconductivity is disrupted by a sufficiently high excitation fluence. We observe this change at electronic temperatures well below the equilibrium superconducting critical temperature. Conversely, when superconductivity is fully restored, the pseudogap is suppressed, as indicated by a particleâhole-symmetric density of states. We also observe the coexistence of pseudogap and superconducting features at intermediate times or intermediate fluence. Our findings challenge the view that superconductivity emerges from phase coherence in the pseudogap. Instead, we show that the two states compete and that the low-temperature ground state of cuprates reflects an interplay between the superconducting and pseudogap states.

item.title: [10] Distinct lattice and charge excitations in AV3Sb5 kagome superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: Stephen D. Wilson, Riccardo Comin

Authors: Dongjin Oh, Stefan Enzner, Lennart Klebl, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: AV3Sb5

Tags: #kagome #AV3Sb5 #CsV3Sb5 #V3Sb5 #chargedensitywave #CDW #superconduct #phonon

Abstract: The kagome superconductor family AV3Sb5 (Aâ=âCs, Rb, K) provides a rich platform for exploring diverse electronic symmetry breaking phenomena, including superconductivity and various forms of density wave orders. Although these compounds share the identical lattice structure in the normal state, they exhibit distinct forms of symmetry breaking upon entering the charge density wave (CDW) phase, and the microscopic origin of which remain elusive. Here, we investigate the lattice and charge degrees of freedom in AV3Sb5 using angle-resolved polarized Raman spectroscopy. Our comprehensive polarization-resolved measurements reveal that the lifting of the twofold-degeneracy of the E2g phonon mode in the CDW phase, previously reported only in CsV3Sb5 with a 3âGHz splitting, also appears ubiquitously in the other two compounds. In contrast, the collective CDW excitations exhibit markedly different polarization dependences depending on the alkali-metal species. These distinct behaviors in the lattice and charge channels provide crucial insight into the enigmatic material-dependent symmetry breaking phenomena that appear in the CDW phase. Furthermore, our experiments, together with first-principles calculations and an effective Hamiltonian model, shed light on the nature of the charge order structure in AV3Sb5 kagome superconductors.

item.title: [9] Altermagnetic signatures and topological textures in ultrathin multiferroic BiFeO3
item.description:
Last authors: Angela Wittmann, Lucas Caretta

Authors: Geo Fratian, Maya Ramesh, Xinyan Li, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Directly features altermagnetism and spin-resolved photoemission, both core interests in the user's profile.

Tags: #spin-resolvedphotoemission #BiFeO3 #altermagnetism

Abstract: Magnetoelectric multiferroics promise low-power switching, non-volatile memory and signal transduction, yet practical deployment requires ultrathin films in which polar and magnetic order often degrade. Uncompensated bound charge drives depolarization in ferroelectrics, whereas off-stoichiometry, reduced anisotropy and charge transfer can produce magnetic dead layers. Here we realize a multiferroic phase of BiFeO3 with no dead layer, revealing signatures of emergent altermagnetism in the ultrathin limit. First-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, atomic-resolution imaging and magnetic imaging show that short-circuit electrostatic boundary conditions and epitaxial strain drive a continuous, thickness-induced phase transition accompanied by multiferroic topological textures. At four unit cells, these boundary conditions stabilize a collinear monoclinic phase with d-wave altermagnetic order, supported by magnetic circular dichroism and spin-resolved photoemission measurements. These results establish a pathway to stabilize unconventional multiferroicity at device-relevant thicknesses, reframing scaling limits for oxide electronics.

item.title: [9] Ultrafast anisotropic valleytronics in SnSe
item.description:
Last authors: Fabio Caruso, Samuel Beaulieu

Authors: Yiming Pan, Sotirios Fragkos, Dominique Descamps, Stéphane Petit, Fabio Caruso, Samuel Beaulieu

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Uses time-resolved ARPES to study electronic dynamics in an anisotropic quantum material.

Tags: #method #tr-ARPES #SnSe

Abstract: Understanding and controlling valley-specific lightâmatter interactions and non-equilibrium microscopic coupling mechanisms lie at the heart of valleytronics. Due to their strong in-plane anisotropy, which enables polarization-controlled optical transitions to distinct non-degenerate valleys, group-IV monochalcogenides have been recently proposed as promising candidates for next-generation valleytronic materials. However, ultrafast non-equilibrium dynamics following the optical preparation of valley-polarized states have received limited attention in these systems. Here, combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with time-dependent Boltzmann equation simulations, we investigate ultrafast valley polarization dynamics following polarization-controlled photoexcitation in SnSe. We show that selective excitation to valleys at global conduction minima yields nearly unity and time-independent valley polarization. By contrast, photoexcitation to the other valley channel leads to ultrafast decay and reversal of valley polarization on subpicosecond timescales due to intervalley scattering mediated by strong electronâphonon coupling with an optical phonon mode. Our findings reveal strongly anisotropic and radically different non-equilibrium valley physics than in most common two-dimensional valleytronics materials.

item.title: [9] Coherent high-velocity chiral magnons in the metallic altermagnet CrSb
item.description:
Last authors: Jonathan Gaudet, Alannah M. Hallas

Authors: Ashutosh K. Singh, Niclas Heinsdorf, Abraham A. Mancilla, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Experimental neutron scattering on a metallic altermagnet, highly relevant to user's interests.

Tags: #experiment #altermagnet #neutronscattering #magnons #CrSb

Abstract: Altermagnets combine the zero net magnetization of antiferromagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting, creating new opportunities for spintronic and magnonic technologies. The full realization of this promise necessitates a material that is simultaneously metallic and altermagnetic, yet preserves the long magnon lifetimes more often seen in insulators. Here, we use polarized neutron diffraction and inelastic neutron scattering to determine the magnetic structure and spin dynamics of the metallic altermagnet CrSb. We confirm a fully compensated, collinear magnetic structure with localized Cr moments and establish the microscopic spin Hamiltonian governing its excitations. Despite its metallicity, CrSb hosts remarkably coherent magnons across its 230 meV bandwidth, with group velocities approaching 60 km/s. Along low-symmetry momentum directions, we resolve chiral magnon splitting generated by higher-order, symmetry-inequivalent exchange interactions, providing the first experimental observation of this phenomenon in a metallic altermagnet. These results reveal a nearly complete separation between magnetic and electronic degrees of freedom in CrSb and demonstrate that metallic transport, room-temperature altermagnetic order, fast coherent magnons, and chiral spin dynamics can coexist in a single material, positioning CrSb as a compelling platform for spintronic applications.
